title: Prefetch reordering causes softmax scaling drift and KV index corruption
creator: Nina Chen
description: Several production inference jobs have returned subtly incorrect token probabilities after we shipped a kernel selection optimization that reorders prefetch operations for the attention fast-path. Failures are low-volume and often only detectable as small softmax scaling differences that can change top-1 outputs for edge prompts. In a few cases we observed KV index mismatches and occasional malformed responses attributed to cache index corruption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy runtime-1.19 with the new kernel selector and prefetch reordering enabled
2) Run a mixed prefill+decode workload with batch sizes 1-4 and sequence lengths that vary (prefill ~512, decode ~64)
3) Use FP16 with q4 fallback quantization profiles enabled on the same machine and stress with concurrent requests to the same model variant
4) Compare token probabilities against a golden run (runtime-1.18) or reference FP32 output and look for >1e-3 KL divergence or top-1 token flips
5) Check server logs for KV index warnings and watch for rare decode where model emits repeated tokens or truncated responses
observed_behavior: Small numerical drift in softmax outputs (1e-4 to 1e-2) across many requests; on rare requests (approx 0.01% under stress) KV cache index corruption leading to misaligned past-key/past-value reads and malformed generations.
expected_behavior: No change in model output distribution beyond acceptable numerical tolerance (<=1e-5 for our regression tests). KV cache indices should remain stable and there should be no malformed generations or repeated tokens introduced by the runtime change.
investigation_summary: Initial bisect points to commit that enabled prefetch operation reordering inside the kernel selector heuristics. Race window exists between prefill-phase write of KV index metadata and decode-phase read when preemptive prefetch moves memory ops earlier. Quantization path (FP16->q4) exposes different rounding which amplified drift. Reproducible in lab with stress harness that forces interleaving of prefill and decode threads. Heap inspection showed KV index table entries transiently point to stale offsets after reorder.
root_cause: The kernel selector's prefetch reordering optimization changed ordering of memory barrier/metadata updates relative to actual KV writes. On machines with weak memory semantics and aggressive concurrency (decode threads swapped onto same core), a read can observe partially-updated KV index pointers. This combined with mixed-precision execution (FP16 + quantized fallback kernels) leads to amplified numerical differences; in worst-case a read of a stale index causes reads from wrong KV slots producing cache corruption symptoms.
mitigation: Rolled back prefetch reordering gate in runtime-1.19 for the default production config (feature-flagged off) and deployed a hotfix to dedicated customers at 2025-02-20. Added an immediate additional memory barrier and atomic update path for KV index writes as a temporary protection on the critical path.
fix_plan: 1) Implement canonical ordering with explicit atomic swap for KV index updates in kernel selector and add unit tested memory serialization primitives. 2) Harden prefetch logic to respect a small state machine (UNINITIALIZED -> WRITING -> VALID) with atomic cas to avoid readers seeing intermediate states. 3) Add deterministic fallback for quantized kernels to avoid mixed-precision ordering differences during handoff. 4) Add stress test harness and deterministic recording to catch regressions in CI.
tests: Add microbenchmark that runs 100k concurrent prefill+decode cycles with randomized scheduling to CI (local-stress suite)
Add numerical regression test that asserts KL divergence < 1e-5 against FP32 golden for a range of prompt shapes
Fuzz KV index metadata transitions with address sanitizer in internal runtime build
deploy_plan: Canary on runtime-1.19-hotfix to 5% of traffic for Dedicated clusters for 48 hours, observe KV-index-warning-rate and KL-divergence histograms, then ramp to 100% if stable. Host public hosted API on patched binary behind routing policy for low-latency slices.
rollout_strategy: Start with non-critical workloads and telemetry-only mode (no auto-rollback) for 24h, then enable full traffic with automatic rollback if KV index errors > 100/day or customer-impacting anomalies observed.
notes: This is prioritized as P0 because of correctness risk even though customer-facing impact is currently rare. The underlying optimization gives ~8% tail-latency improvement in internal benchmarks; we want to re-enable it once correctness is proven.
